bug_semantics: The keyserver and telemetry FastAPI POST /refresh handlers bind the bearer-like refresh_token secret with Query(...), so clients must put a credential that can mint a new access/refresh pair into the request URL. URLs are routinely retained by origin/proxy access logs, browser history, Referer propagation, and network-monitoring systems; anyone who recovers the token can submit it to refresh_access_token(), which validates its type and subject and issues a fresh token pair for that client, enabling unauthorized access.
flaw_origin: Commit cdc9c7d814915a9a2c568987b7bcc14f3b7cf533 introduced the refresh-token feature and, in the same smallest feature commit, created both vulnerable handlers at openssl_encrypt_server/modules/keyserver/routes.py:213-216 and openssl_encrypt_server/modules/telemetry/routes.py:89-92 with the exact parameter `refresh_token: str = Query(..., description="Refresh token")`. Its direct parent e5961e7a72b3e37bad6012ff2c06aeacefb85aca contains neither refresh handler nor that vulnerable query binding.

`git log --all --reverse -S'refresh_token: str = Query(..., description="Refresh token")' -- openssl_encrypt_server/modules/keyserver/routes.py openssl_encrypt_server/modules/telemetry/routes.py` first returns cdc9c7d814915a9a2c568987b7bcc14f3b7cf533. `git log -L 213,216:openssl_encrypt_server/modules/keyserver/routes.py v1.4.0` attributes all four vulnerable handler-signature lines to that commit; `git log -L 96,99:openssl_encrypt_server/modules/telemetry/routes.py v1.4.0` traces the replaced Query line through fix 4b2adb05cde8a7ee03cdd271755da3b377c68011 back to the same BIC. Commit URL: https://github.com/jahlives/openssl_encrypt/commit/cdc9c7d814915a9a2c568987b7bcc14f3b7cf533.

Direct-parent tree check `git grep -n -E 'async def refresh_token|refresh_token: str = Query' cdc9c7d814915a9a2c568987b7bcc14f3b7cf533^ -- openssl_encrypt_server/modules/keyserver/routes.py openssl_encrypt_server/modules/telemetry/routes.py` returns no matches. The BIC is a single-parent, cohesive refresh-token implementation commit whose sole parent is full SHA e5961e7a72b3e37bad6012ff2c06aeacefb85aca; it is not a merge, move, revert, release aggregation, or reconstructable squash.

At the BIC, openssl_encrypt_server/core/auth/token.py:201-241 implements refresh_access_token(): it verifies the supplied secret, enforces token type `refresh`, uses the token subject as client_id, and calls create_token_pair(). Both new routes pass the URL-bound value to that function and return the new access and refresh tokens, establishing the credential-theft attack path rather than merely a logging concern.

Direct fix commit https://github.com/jahlives/openssl_encrypt/commit/4b2adb05cde8a7ee03cdd271755da3b377c68011 changes openssl_encrypt_server/modules/telemetry/routes.py from Query(...) to `body: RefreshRequest = Body(...)` and passes body.refresh_token to the authenticator. Its full parent is 7aa8787f4de2e9a23f58fca067bb16c4c69d28bb. This is the advisory-named semantic fix, but its one-file diff does not fix the keyserver route.

Version cross-check: `git tag --contains cdc9c7d814915a9a2c568987b7bcc14f3b7cf533` starts at v1.4.0 (and includes v1.4.0rc1/v1.4.0rc2), while v1.3.6 has no refresh handler; the BIC tree's setup.py reports VERSION = `1.4.0`. `git tag --contains 4b2adb05cde8a7ee03cdd271755da3b377c68011` likewise includes v1.4.0rc1, v1.4.0rc2, and v1.4.0, so the telemetry correction is present at the declared stable patched boundary. Release evidence: https://github.com/jahlives/openssl_encrypt/releases/tag/v1.4.0.

The claimed boundary is incomplete for keyserver: `git grep` at v1.4.0 and v1.4.1 still finds openssl_encrypt_server/modules/keyserver/routes.py:215 binding refresh_token with Query(...), while telemetry uses RefreshRequest/Body. No advisory-keyed or content-search fix changes the keyserver binding. Commit bf5e4d81037fa1b41e65c3fc17007782939e64fc later deletes the entire openssl_encrypt_server subtree as a repository extraction and is first contained by v1.4.2; deletion/move is not a direct vulnerability fix.
reasoning: The vulnerable mechanism did not exist in the direct parent. The January 3 refresh-token feature commit cdc9c7d814915a9a2c568987b7bcc14f3b7cf533 simultaneously added the sensitive token type, the renewal method, and both externally reachable refresh endpoints, and chose FastAPI Query binding for the secret. Line history and pickaxe converge on that focused single-parent commit, so no later refactor, release commit, or removal supplants it as the smallest BIC. The first-party advisory's 4b2adb05cde8a7ee03cdd271755da3b377c68011 correction proves the intended safe design—POST-body binding—but fixes only telemetry. Stable versions before v1.4.0 lack the newly introduced handler, and v1.4.0 contains both the BIC and telemetry fix; however, its keyserver route (and v1.4.1's) remains vulnerable, making the published `< 1.4.0` / `1.4.0` boundary only partially true. Attribution is decided solely from the BIC commit object: its explicit Claude Code generation line and Claude Sonnet 4.5 co-author trailer directly cover the commit that first wrote both flawed handlers. That causal and commit-object linkage satisfies AI_ROOT_CAUSE regardless of the later fix's provenance.
